lead.zh-Hans: 故宫里的一小段等待，被我装进了信里。
lead.en: A short wait at the Forbidden City found its way into this letter.

text.zh-Hans: 在北京故宫看过殿宇和园林，我停下来等一位约好的旅人。每听见一阵脚步，我就抬一下头，结果先认出了自己的邮包拉链声。等对方来了，我说今天的路已经听过两遍：一遍走过，一遍等过。明天给这段等待留个名字。
text.en: After visiting the palace buildings and gardens of Beijing’s Forbidden City, I waited for a traveler I had arranged to meet. Every set of footsteps made me look up. The first sound I recognized was actually my own mailbag zipper. When my friend arrived, I said I had heard the route twice: once while walking, once while waiting. Tomorrow this little wait needs a name.

text.zh-Hans: 问问旅人会给等待起什么名
text.en: Ask the traveler for a name for the wait

text.zh-Hans: 把等人的声音记下来
text.en: Keep a note of the sounds while waiting

lead.zh-Hans: 在颐和园，我把一句话停在了湖面上。
lead.en: At the Summer Palace, a sentence paused over the water.

text.zh-Hans: 颐和园的山、水和亭台连在一起，我原本想给每一样写个词。写到湖面，却停了下来，坐着看了一会儿。回头读便签，山和亭台之间竟有一大段停顿。我没有填满它，只加了一个小逗号。明天看看，这个逗号是不是也想继续歇脚。
text.en: The Summer Palace brought hills, water and pavilions into one view. I began a word for each, then reached the lake and simply sat for a while. My note now has a long pause between the hills and the buildings. I added one small comma and left it there. Tomorrow I will check whether the comma is still enjoying its rest.

text.zh-Hans: 请同行人接着说下一句
text.en: Invite a companion to finish the sentence

text.zh-Hans: 看看停顿两边各有什么
text.en: Notice what sits on either side of the pause

lead.zh-Hans: 烤鸭菜单上，第一行先写成了“再来一口”。
lead.en: The first line on my duck menu said, “Another bite.”

text.zh-Hans: 在北京吃烤鸭，我尝了用薄饼包起来的一份。想写菜单的时候，脑袋还留在刚才那一口，笔下先跑出“再来一口”。我把菜名补在旁边，保留了原来那句。这样就算把菜单拿倒，至少还能读出我的心情。明天得把它放正再收进邮包。
text.en: In Beijing I tried Peking duck wrapped in a thin pancake. When I reached for my menu card, my thoughts were still busy with lunch. “Another bite” appeared before the dish’s name did. I added the name beside it and kept both. Even upside down, this menu should convey my opinion. Tomorrow I will pack it the right way up.

text.zh-Hans: 给这行开场白找个听众
text.en: Find someone to read the opening line

text.zh-Hans: 看看菜名和那句话谁先入眼
text.en: See which line catches your eye first

lead.zh-Hans: 面条先拌好了，句子稍后再拌。
lead.en: The noodles were mixed before the sentence was.

text.zh-Hans: 北京炸酱面的面条、炸酱和菜码到了眼前，我先放下笔，把这一碗拌好再吃。回来写菜单时，竟差点把顺序写成“拌信、吃笔”。我重新写了张便条：先拌面，再写信。旧的也留着，明天提醒自己别让铅笔抢了午饭的位置。
text.en: With noodles, sauce and vegetable accompaniments in front of me, I put my pencil down and mixed my zhajiang noodles. Back at the menu card, I nearly wrote “mix the letter, eat the pencil.” A fresh slip now gives clearer instructions: noodles first, letter second. I kept the muddled version too. Tomorrow the pencil can have a quieter job.

text.zh-Hans: 念一遍这张顺序便条
text.en: Read the little sequence aloud

text.zh-Hans: 找出旧便条里换错的位置
text.en: Spot the swapped words on the old slip

lead.zh-Hans: 两张北京菜单，今天有了自己的朗读会。
lead.en: Two Beijing menu cards held a tiny reading session.

text.zh-Hans: 今天分两顿尝了烤鸭和炸酱面，我把两张小菜单拿给一位旅人看。对方先读“再来一口”，再读“先拌面，再写信”，说像一封被午饭打断的信。我索性请对方替它们排个顺序，最后我们各写一张次序条。明天换着读，看看哪份更像我的一天。
text.en: I tried Peking duck at one meal and zhajiang noodles at another, then showed a traveler both menu cards. “Another bite,” followed by “noodles first, letter second,” sounded to them like correspondence interrupted by lunch. We each wrote an order for reading the cards. Tomorrow I will try both arrangements and see which sounds more like my day.

text.zh-Hans: 替两张菜单再排一次顺序
text.en: Suggest another order for the cards

text.zh-Hans: 看看两张次序条有何不同
text.en: Compare our two reading orders

lead.zh-Hans: 从“吃”走到“写”，今天只隔着两张菜单。
lead.en: Today the distance from eating to writing was two menu cards.

text.zh-Hans: 在北京，我先后尝了薄饼包着的烤鸭和拌好的炸酱面。两张菜单摆在桌上，我才发现自己写了好多动词：包、拌、吃、写。于是把这些字抄成一小条路，末尾添上“收好”。最后一个词倒提醒了我，两张菜单还摊着呢。明天再看看，路上有没有漏掉“歇歇”。
text.en: After Peking duck in a pancake and a bowl of mixed zhajiang noodles, I laid out the two menu cards. They were full of busy little verbs: wrap, mix, eat, write. I copied the words into a trail and ended it with “pack.” A useful reminder, since both cards were still on the table. Tomorrow I will see where “rest” belongs along the way.

text.zh-Hans: 给这条词语小路加个路口
text.en: Add a turning to the word trail

text.zh-Hans: 看看哪个词走在最后
text.en: Check which word brings up the rear

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，我把那段等待重新听了一遍。
lead.en: Your “{reply}” sent me back to that little wait.

text.zh-Hans: 我把在故宫等人的声音记下了：脚步近一点，停一停，邮包拉链轻轻一响。读出来不像一段路线，倒像一句还没讲完的话。我给便签起名“快到了”，下面留着一行空白。下回等朋友时，就从那里接着记，看看结尾会不会是笑声。
text.en: My Forbidden City waiting note now reads: footsteps nearer, a pause, the soft zip of a mailbag. Read aloud, it sounds less like directions than an unfinished sentence. I named the slip “Nearly here” and left a line below it. The next time I wait for a friend, I can continue there. Perhaps the ending will be a laugh.

text.zh-Hans: 为这段声音念个开场
text.en: Give the sounds a spoken introduction

text.zh-Hans: 留意最后那行空白
text.en: Keep an eye on the final empty line
